subtype: Approach: spend freely and see what is left [Pitfall]
passage: In Lagos, Chidi's first pay landed on a Friday, and by Saturday it felt like a fortune. Chidi bought the newest phone on monthly instalments, ate out with colleagues four nights a week, and ordered a new jacket online. Nobody had said no, and no total had ever been set for the month. Sami, sharing the flat, saw the bags arriving and said nothing at first. By the twentieth, the account was empty. Chidi borrowed from Sami for the bus fare and skipped the office lunch. The phone instalment was due in five days. Sitting on the kitchen floor, Chidi wrote the same question three times on a napkin: where did it all go?

qa.q: On which day of the month was the account empty?
qa.a: The account was empty by the twentieth.

qa.q: What was Chidi feeling while writing the question on the napkin?
qa.a: Chidi was confused and anxious about where the money had gone, since no total had been set for the month.

qa.q: What could Chidi do at the start of next month, and why?
qa.a: Chidi could set a total for the month and list the bills first, because a limit shows what is safe to spend.

qa.q: How might Sami see lending money for the bus fare?
qa.a: Sami may feel worried and a little uneasy, since Sami saw the bags arrive and now sees the empty account.

grounding: A first-job employee treats the credited amount as plentiful, buys a phone on instalments and eats out often, and runs out before month's end.

subtype: Approach: spend freely and see what is left [Pitfall]
passage:
On the 20th, at the office cafeteria, Jasleen's card was declined for a ₹90 thali. She tried again. Declined.
Irawati, who sat next to her in the claims team, paid without comment. Back at their desks, Jasleen opened her bank app and scrolled up. The ₹32,000 salary had come on the 1st. On the 2nd, the new phone: ₹3,800 EMI for twelve months. Then the team dinner, the weekend café, delivery almost every night because the office ran late, a new jacket, a cab whenever it rained. No single thing had felt big.
'I never actually decided how much I'd spend,' she said quietly. 'I just thought it was a lot.'
Irawati nodded. 'Ten days till next salary?'
'Eleven.' Jasleen closed the app. The phone EMI would come out again on the 2nd, whether she ate or not.

qa.q: What was Jasleen feeling when she said 'I just thought it was a lot'?
qa.a: Embarrassed and anxious, seeing that the money had gone with no total ever set and eleven days still to go.

qa.q: Which approach would have suited Jasleen better at the start of the month?
qa.a: Listing fixed costs like the EMI, setting a total for everything else and checking it each week, instead of spending until it ran out.

qa.q: What is it like for Irawati when the card is declined?
qa.a: Irawati quietly covers the thali to spare Jasleen embarrassment, and asks about payday instead of judging.

grounding: Shows a first-job employee spending freely after salary, buying a phone on EMI and eating out, until the account is empty by the 20th.

subtype: Approach: spend freely and see what is left [Pitfall]
passage:
Subject: embarrassing, but I need to talk

Lalit bhaiya,
Twenty days into my first job and my account shows ₹640. I wanted to tell you before Mummy hears it from someone else.
When the ₹29,000 came in on the 1st, it felt endless. I bought the phone I'd wanted since college, on EMI, ₹2,900 a month for a year. I took the new team out on my first Friday, because that's what seniors did for me. Momos, rolls, coffee every evening after the shift. Two movies. I never wrote a number anywhere. I thought, it's a salary, it'll last.
Rent is due on the 25th. I'm not asking for money yet. I'm asking if you'll sit with me on Sunday and help me make an actual plan, because clearly I never had one.
Gautam

qa.q: What does Gautam's account show twenty days into the job?
What might Gautam be worried about in writing this email?
qa.a: Gautam is anxious about the rent due on the 25th and ashamed enough to want Lalit to know before Mummy hears.

qa.q: What should the plan Gautam asks for start with?
qa.a: Listing fixed costs like rent and the phone EMI first, then setting a total for everything else and checking it through the month.

qa.q: How might Lalit feel reading the email?
qa.a: Lalit may be concerned but also glad to be trusted, since Gautam is asking for help planning, not only for money.

grounding: Shows a first-job employee who spent freely with no monthly total and found the account nearly empty by the 20th.
